evidence.claim: Farm country, a working mill and a river crossing atop a dam
evidence.quote: life “down on the farm.”

evidence.claim: a working mill
evidence.quote: The working grist mill offers a fascinating window into centuries-old technology.

evidence.claim: a river crossing atop a dam
evidence.quote: crosses the Susquehanna River on the Conowingo Dam.

evidence.claim: The Mason and Dixon Scenic Byway runs through rural Maryland just south of the Pennsylvania boundary.
evidence.quote: The Mason and Dixon Scenic Byway runs south of the Mason–Dixon line, a line surveyed by Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon in the 1760s to separate Maryland from Pennsylvania.

evidence.claim: Maryland’s tourism office presents this state scenic drive as a journey through farm country, historical sites and outdoor recreation.
evidence.quote: On this easy-going drive along country vistas just south of the Pennsylvania border, prepare yourself for historical encounters, recreational endeavors and life “down on the farm.”

evidence.claim: Its landscape includes Prettyboy Reservoir, the rocky forest of Rocks State Park and the Susquehanna crossing at Conowingo Dam.
evidence.quote: The park has 855 acres of rocky forest land

evidence.claim: The name recalls Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon, whose survey in the 1760s separated Maryland from Pennsylvania.
evidence.quote: a line surveyed by Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon in the 1760s to separate Maryland from Pennsylvania.

evidence.claim: A later engineering project changed the route across the Susquehanna: Conowingo Dam’s reservoir would cover the old U.S. 1 bridge, which was demolished in 1927.
evidence.quote: The rising water also would have covered Conowingo Bridge, the original U.S. Route 1 crossing, so it was demolished in 1927.

evidence.claim: U.S. 1 now crosses the top of the dam, while the reservoir covers the original town of Conowingo.
evidence.quote: The dam supports a 9,000-acre reservoir, which today covers the original town of Conowingo.

evidence.claim: Start in Westminster and head north to Union Mills, then east through Manchester toward Prettyboy Reservoir.
evidence.quote: From Westminster, the byway heads north on MD 97 to Union Mills

evidence.claim: Beyond White Hall, a side loop reaches Rocks State Park and Deer Creek.
evidence.quote: In Harkins, a loop of the Mason and Dixon Scenic Byway heads south on MD 24, passing Eden Mill Nature Center and Rocks State Park.

evidence.claim: Return to the main route for the crossing on Conowingo Dam, then continue through Rising Sun and past Fair Hill’s equestrian grounds to Appleton at the Delaware border.
evidence.quote: The road comes to the Fair Hill Natural Resource Management Area, which occupies former land owned by the Du Pont family and has equestrian facilities, before the byway ends at the Delaware border in Appleton.

evidence.claim: Its landscape includes Prettyboy Reservoir
evidence.quote: heads across the Prettyboy Reservoir.

evidence.claim: U.S. 1 now crosses the top of the dam
evidence.quote: U.S. Route 1 now crosses over the top of the dam.

evidence.claim: then east through Manchester toward Prettyboy Reservoir
evidence.quote: The Mason and Dixon Scenic byway splits east onto Beckleysville Road and heads across the Prettyboy Reservoir.

evidence.claim: then east through Manchester
evidence.quote: passing through Melrose before reaching Manchester, a historic town.

evidence.claim: Beyond White Hall
evidence.quote: From here, the Mason and Dixon Scenic Byway continues along White Hall Road, turning north onto MD 23

evidence.claim: Rocks State Park and Deer Creek
evidence.quote: Rocks State Park is a Maryland state park located in and around Deer Creek Valley

evidence.claim: continue through Rising Sun
evidence.quote: The Mason and Dixon Scenic Byway heads east onto MD 273 and passes through Rising Sun

evidence.claim: The brick gristmill at Union Mills dates to 1797, the same year Andrew and David Shriver built their homestead.
evidence.quote: The Shriver Homestead was built in 1797 by Andrew and David Shriver

evidence.claim: Locally made bricks form its walls, laid in both Flemish and common bond.
evidence.quote: The mill, also built in 1797, is a large brick structure, built of locally manufactured brick laid in both Flemish bond and common bond.

evidence.claim: In June 1863, part of the Shriver family hosted Confederate General J.E.B. Stuart; the next day, other family members welcomed Union General James Barnes.
evidence.quote: On June 30, 1863, General J.E.B. Stuart of the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia camped at Union Mills and was hosted by part of the Shriver family. On the following day, General James Barnes of the 5th Corps of the Army of the Potomac arrived on the site and welcomed and entertained by other members of the family.

evidence.claim: The homestead is now a museum, and the mill still works.
evidence.quote: Built in 1797 and now a museum, Union Mills has a remarkable history.

evidence.claim: The complex also contains a surviving tannery bark shed and a reconstructed tannery barn, two different kinds of evidence of its industrial past.
evidence.quote: a surviving bark shed from the 19th century tannery complex, a reconstructed tannery barn

evidence.claim: Locally made brick forms the mill walls in Flemish and common bond.
evidence.quote: built of locally manufactured brick laid in both Flemish bond and common bond.

evidence.claim: the mill still works
evidence.quote: The working grist mill

evidence.claim: The King and Queen’s Seat rises 190 feet above the banks of Deer Creek in Rocks State Park.
evidence.quote: a 190-foot (58 m) rock outcropping that towers above the banks of Deer Creek.

evidence.claim: Visitors were coming to the Rocks of Deer Creek in the nineteenth century, when the Maryland and Pennsylvania Railroad served the attraction.
evidence.quote: The “Rocks of Deer Creek” were already a tourist attraction in the 19th century, served by the Maryland and Pennsylvania Railroad at milepost 35.3 until 1958.

evidence.claim: The state bought 82 acres here in 1949 and opened Deer Creek State Park in 1953.
evidence.quote: The state purchased 82 acres at the site in 1949, opening it under the name Deer Creek State Park in 1953.

evidence.claim: The park now has three separate sections in the valley. The outcrop belongs to the largest, along Rocks Ridge; Kilgore Falls lies in the separate Falling Branch section.
evidence.quote: The park has three noncontiguous sections in Deer Creek Valley. The largest section, home to park headquarters, is located along Rocks Ridge

evidence.claim: The rock outcrop towers above the banks of Deer Creek.
evidence.quote: rock outcropping that towers above the banks of Deer Creek.

evidence.claim: Kilgore Falls lies in the separate Falling Branch section.
evidence.quote: It is home to Kilgore Falls, the second highest waterfall in Maryland.

evidence.claim: Fair Hill’s protected land was once part of William duPont, Jr.’s holdings.
evidence.quote: a 5,613 acre protected area formerly part of the land holdings of William duPont, Jr.

evidence.claim: Its long equestrian use gained a thoroughbred training center in 1983.
evidence.quote: It has long been an area used by equestrians. The Fair Hill Training Center for thoroughbred horses was built on the site in 1983.

evidence.claim: The natural resources management area has 80 miles of trails, fishing areas and a nature center.
evidence.quote: It has 80 miles of trails. Fishing areas are available. There is a nature center and ruins to explore.

evidence.claim: Near the Fair Hill Nature and Environmental Center is the Foxcatcher Farm Covered Bridge, one of two covered bridges in Cecil County.
evidence.quote: The Foxcatcher Farm Covered Bridge, which is one of two covered bridges in Cecil County, is located on the property near the Fair Hill Nature and Environmental Center.

evidence.claim: The Foxcatcher Farm Covered Bridge stands near the nature center.
evidence.quote: The Foxcatcher Farm Covered Bridge, which is one of two covered bridges in Cecil County, is located on the property near the Fair Hill Nature and Environmental Center.

evidence.claim: Manchester lies in rolling upland on the Piedmont Plateau, west of the Chesapeake Bay’s coastal lowlands.
evidence.quote: Manchester is located on the Piedmont Plateau, west of the coastal lowlands of the Chesapeake Bay, in an area of rolling upland.

evidence.claim: Their boundary work helped settle a land dispute involving Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia and Delaware.
evidence.quote: Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon spent nearly four years helping to settle a land dispute by surveying newly established boundaries between Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia and Delaware.

evidence.claim: Across the park, 3.5 miles of hiking trails offer views of this landscape.
evidence.quote: The park offers scenic views on 3.5 miles (5.6 km) of hiking trails
